name: OSMTracker
tagline: Record a GPS track with notes, photos and voice memos
description:
OSMTracker logs where you walk, ride or drive, and lets you mark things as you pass them. The big buttons on the main screen are for tagging what you see — a bench, a gate, a junction — and you can also take a photo, record a voice note or type a comment straight into the track.

Everything ends up in a GPX file you can export. It was made for people who add detail to OpenStreetMap, but it works just as well for keeping a record of a hike or surveying somewhere new.

The button layout is fully customisable, so you can set it up for whatever you are actually out there mapping.
